correctness.rationale: For real -1<=B<A<=1, odd normalization and a complex Schwarz subordination reduce to an even Schwarz function v(z²), since the Janowski Möbius map is injective. Parity splits T6 into two identical symmetric 3x3 blocks, giving D=(1-a5)(1+a5-2a3²) and T6=D². Write d=A-B, R=|u|², t=u², v2=(1-R)eta: a3=d u/2, a5=k t+ell(1-R)eta, k=d(A-3B)/8, m=d(3A-B)/8, ell=d/4. Expanding D gives 1-St+Kt²+ell(m-k)t(1-R)eta-ell²(1-R)²eta², S=d²/2, K=km. Independently factored the symbolic identity. Angular derivative of |1-St+Kt²|² in cos(arg t) is negative on [-1,1] using K>=-S/8 and S<=2, hence unique t=-R for R>0. The quantitative radial bound P(-1)-|D|>=(1-R)3d²/16 forces R=1. Then v(zeta)=u zeta, u=+i or -i, yielding unique f± and squared bound ((8+d(A-3B))(8+d(3A-B))/64)^2; at (1,-1) it is 16. Equality, nondegeneracy d>0, endpoints B=0 and B=-1, and symmetric-not-Hermitian normalization are all checked. The package script confirms identities/finite meshes only; the arbitrary-parameter proof is the strict analytic angular/radial inequality.
residual_risks: The proof applies only to symmetric Toeplitz determinant of odd class; no complex lower extremum or general q is claimed.
One must not confuse a verifier sampling 40,000 Schwarz points with a proof of the global bound.

value.rationale: The parameter-uniform exact extremal constant with a full equality classification resolves a natural open problem in a recently published Toeplitz-class classification. It demonstrates a global real-versus-complex discontinuity for the SAME Janowski parameters, from real maximum 1 to >1 for every d>0, reaching 16 at a natural starlike endpoint. This is not merely symbolic expansion of a known bound; the strict two-complex-variable Schur optimization supplies the missing result.
residual_risks: Value is confined to odd sixth-order symmetric determinants and does not address Hermitian or all normalizations.
